results.title: Toasts overview  |  Android Developers
excerpts:
* [Android Developers](https://developer.android.com/)

# Toasts overview

A toast provides simple feedback about an operation in a small popup. It only
fills the amount of space required for the message and the current activity
remains visible and interactive. Toasts automatically disappear after a timeout.

For example, clicking **Send** on an email triggers a "Sending message..."
toast, as shown in the following screen capture:

Image of Android device showing a toast popup reading
            'Sending message' next to an app icon

If your app targets Android 12 (API level 31) or higher, its toast is limited to
two lines of text and shows the application icon next to the text. Be aware that
the line length of this text varies by screen size, so it's good to make the
text as short as possible.

## Alternatives to using toasts

If your app is in the foreground, consider using a [snackbar](https://material.io/components/snackbars) instead of using a toast.

## What is a toast component?

Toasts display brief, temporary messages. They're meant to be **noticed without disrupting a user's attention** , and it should automatically disappear afterwards.

Think of it like a piece of toast popping up from a toaster - it pops up then goes back down.

Toasts are commonly seen in design patterns such as: [Acknowledgement](https://mobbin.com/search/ios/screens?filter=screenPatterns.Acknowledgement+%26+Success_screenElements.Toast) or [Error handling](https://mobbin.com/search/ios/screens?filter=screenElements.

...

If you require a message to remain visible, consider using a Banner instead.

## What is the anatomy of a toast component?

Anatomy of a toast

1

Container

2

Supporting icon (optional)

3

Supporting text

4

Action button (optional)

5

Close button (optional)

## What are the design variants of a toast?

We studied over [**2,500+ toast ui components on Mobbin**](https://mobbin.com/search/ios/ui-elements?filter=screenElements.Toast) , from real-world examples and found the following variants.

### Placement

Mobile toast components are typically positioned above the content along the Y-axis (bottom, center, top alignment).

Top aligned toasts on mobile.

Center aligned toast on mobile.

Bottom aligned toast on mobile.

In web layouts, designers can consider utilizing horizontal alignment (left, center, right), taking advantage of the expanded screen real estate compared to mobile interfaces.

### Form
Depending on a brand's design system - there are 3 basic forms: Bar, Full-bleed, and Box.

Box-style toast UI.

Full-bleed style toast UI.

Bar-style toast UI (with different border radiuses)

### Follow up action buttons

When adding an action button on a mobile app, bottom placement is ideal for easy thumb reach.

Bottom placement toasts with CTA button.

### Caret tip

You can consider adding caret tips to your toasts if you need to directionally nudge users. However, this is not commonly used as a toast as it resembles a **Tooltip** .

Toasts with carets that look like tooltips.

## When to use a toast?

### Success & acknowledgment

After a user performs an action, such as submitting a form or deleting an item, a toast can be used to confirm the action's successful completion. They usually use a positive semantic color (i.e: green), which indicates that an action has been successfully completed.

...

### Toast v.s. Banners

Toasts are intended to be short, non-intrusive notifications that usually quickly disappear from the screen after a few seconds. Toasts also do not persist as the user navigates through different pages of the app.

In situations where you need information to persist, you should use a **Banner** instead.

Examples of banners

### Toast v.s. Tooltips

Tooltips are typically used to provide more detailed information about an element or to provide instructions on how to use the element.

Instead, toasts are typically used to provide brief feedback to an action taken by the user.

In situations where you want to give users more context or instructions, you should use a [Tooltip](https://mobbin.com/glossary/mobbin.com/glossary/tooltips) instead.

Examples of tooltips

## Top 5 Twitch Overlay Types A Streamer Needs To Maximize Engagement

# Highlight Your Stream

### Webcam Boxes & Chat Boxes

**What are Webcam Boxes and Chat Boxes?:**

* Cam borders for your webcam stream, chat boxes from intermission scenes and any labels to showcase latest events such as subscribers, followers and so on.

**Why do Webcam Boxes and Chat Boxes matter?:**

* Structure your stream with these important Twitch overlays to present a professional look to your viewers.
* Keep your stream structured by separating sections using frames.
* Create focus on different areas of your stream, drawing attention to parts that you want to showcase.
* Grab viewer attention and make sure your stream is clutter free.

**Streamer tips for using Webcam Boxes and Chat Boxes:**

* Keep them minimal and interesting, whilst bearing in mind that your Twitch overlays should not overtake the actual content.
* When creating your brand, you want your Twitch overlays to be consistent and to flow with your other designs.
* Animated webcam boxes and chat boxes give an extra layer of dynamic movement to your stream and are more visually interesting and engaging for your viewers.

# Hype Up Your Stream

see more

### Hype Train Widgets & Goal Bar Widgets

**What are Hype Train Widgets & Goal Bar Widgets?:**

* Goal Bar widgets are used by the streamer to set a goal to work towards - usually number of followers, subscribers or donations.
* Hype Train widgets show the progression towards a set goal to build interest and hype in the chosen goal.
* Both show real time updates to track progress with.

**Why do Hype Train Widgets & Goal Bar Widgets matter?:**

* Both of these Twitch overlays visually display a goal that you are working towards to your viewers. Displaying your goals on stream using widgets creates an interest in the goals itself.
* Drives engagement with the goal to build upon the hype with your community.
* Gets your viewers to interact with your stream to push you towards the chosen goal by following, subscribing or donating.

**Streamer tips for using Hype Train Widgets & Goal Bar Widgets:**

* Make sure your goal is achievable and believable - this will make your viewers more likely to contribute.
* Connect your goal to a celebration for when you fulfil it such as alerts, or content related such as special events or challenges.
* Use sparingly and not clutter your screen.

# Interact With Your Stream

see more

### Animated Alerts

**What are Animated Alerts?:**

* Animated Alerts are dynamic motion designs that signify an event or trigger has been fulfilled, that then notifies the stream of the achievement. For example, new follows, subscribers, bits, superchats, members and so forth.
* These Twitch overlays come in several different types - animated alerts and 3D animated alerts.
Both are available in a range of designs, and 3D alerts tend to be for bigger celebrations and wins.

**Why do Animated Alerts matter?:**

* Animated Alerts instantly confirm and recognize viewer interactions. This both acknowledges the trigger that came from the viewer and indirectly thanks them for their contribution.
* Between the pop up animations, the visual stimulation and seeing their name on your stream - viewers will be encouraged to keep interacting to trigger more alerts.

**Streamer tip for using Animated Alerts:**

* Keep your alerts on theme for your branding, quick and impactful as to not block your content.
* Consider 3D chest alerts for bigger celebrations.

# Structure Your Stream

see more

### Countdown Timers Widgets

**What are Countdown Timer Widgets?:**

* Countdown Timer Widgets display a timer on your stream that counts down using a timer you set to an event of your choosing.
* These Twitch overlays can be used over the top of content or other overlays such as starting soon screens.

**Why do Countdown Timers matter?:**

* Using a timer keeps your viewers engaged in your stream.
* Signify when events are starting by giving your audience a wait time that will mean they do not click off your stream.
* Countdown widgets can be used to signify when a stream is starting, when you are returning from a break, community events, time left before a challenge finishes and more.

**Streamer tips for using Countdown Timers?:**

* Use your timers constructively and at appropriate times so they are more impactful.
* Make sure that your style of countdown timer matches the rest of your Twitch overlays.
* Countdown timers are ideal for if you need to take a break to keep your viewers watching whilst you are not on screen.
